text:
elena (design): Draft concept for a compressed latency header — single-line toolbar so the heatmap has more vertical space on small screens. Main pieces: presets (15s/1m/10m/1h), a compact 'Custom' chevron that opens the full picker, a collapsed 'Sampling' chip that expands to a micro-slider, and a persistent p95 pill on the right. Figma: https://figma.com/file/latency-header-ex pete (frontend): This looks promising. Couple of frontend notes: (1) the sampling chip should show a small badge when non-default (dot or percent), (2) expansion should avoid layout shift (use transform + absolute overlay). jules (eng): Backend constraints: sampling changes hit different aggregation paths. Please include sampling_pct in the route and debounce slider updates on the client (200ms). Also suggest logging `toolbar_preset` and `sampling_change` events for analytics. katie (pm): Product context: users often switch presets during incident triage. We should make presets tappable and expose keyboard shortcuts for last-used presets. Default sampling for most orgs = 20% to balance cost/detail. We'll track preset vs custom to choose better defaults later. sam (a11y): Accessibility points: presets must be focusable and announce the selection; use role=listbox or tablist depending on pattern. The sampling slider needs aria-valuetext ("Sampling: 20%"), and the chart re-render should be announced via aria-live polite with short phrasing like "Latency chart updated to 1 minute range". Also color contrast on the tiny legend chips is low in dark theme at 12px; bump contrast or increase size. elena (design): For discoverability, I propose: keep presets visible, collapse sampling into a pill with a chevron, and show a tiny inline help icon that on hover says: "Sampling reduces processing and storage; may hide small spikes." We'll A/B test wording: that vs "Sampling reduces detail but saves compute." pete (frontend): Implementation sketch (simplified): ```
\n
[15s][1m][10m][1h]
\n \n \n
p95: 120ms
\n
``` Expanded sampling shows an `input[type=range]` with `aria-valuetext` and a visible dot when changed from default. We'll debounce network calls and update URL with `?sampling_pct=20` so links are shareable. jules (eng): Good. Additional infra ask: server should compute p95 only on range change, cache it for 1s, and expose a lightweight endpoint for p95 to avoid heavy chart recompute on every hover. That will keep the UI snappy. katie (pm): Decision: ship v1 with the compact toolbar, presets, custom picker, collapsed sampling chip (default 20%), pinned p95. Follow-ups: a11y checklist from Sam, telemetry events from Jules, prototype from Pete, and copy variants for the tooltip from Elena. sam (a11y): I'll draft the a11y checklist: keyboard flow, listbox semantics, aria-live examples, slider aria patterns, tooltip semantics, and contrast targets. Will ping once done. ops-bot: Note: branch `feature/compact-latency-header` created by pete at 1972004500. pete (frontend): I'll prototype the collapsed chip with expand animation (scale + fade) and add a low-density overlay for sampling <=5% that shows a badge "low sampling expect noise" and a subtle crosshatch pattern on cells for colorblind support. ETA: Thursday. elena (design): Thanks all — I'll update mocks with contrast tweaks and include both micro-copy options for the sampling tooltip for the UX sync. :sparkles:
